docs.summary: Fluent builder for a generic, host-agnostic node graph. The widget is a pure view + intent emitter: it never mutates the graph. Every edit is raised as an event (with enough data to build an undo step); the host applies it to its own model and records undo. Nodes are real Paper elements; grid, wires and ports are drawn on the canvas from the same pan/zoom used to place the nodes, so everything stays frame-perfect.

members.signature: public NodeGraphBuilder Size(float width, float height)

docs.summary: Disable node/group/sticky/wire editing (move, resize, connect, delete, rename) while keeping pan, zoom, and selection active — a view-only inspection mode.

The host handles delete and select all through its own shortcut system, calling [`DeleteSelection`](#api~Prowl.OrigamiUI.NodeGraphController~DeleteSelection) and [`SelectAll`](#api~Prowl.OrigamiUI.NodeGraphController~SelectAll), so the widget stops answering its fixed keys for them. Escape still clears the selection.

Snap dragged nodes to a grid of this size (graph space). 0 turns snapping off.
Let a wire run from a node back into itself, leaving the decision to the validator.

The collapse chevron on a node was clicked. Host flips [`Collapsed`](#api~Prowl.OrigamiUI.GraphNode~Collapsed).

A wire was pulled off its input port. The host removes it; if the drag then lands on another port, `OnConnect` follows with the new one. Without this handler a connected input starts a fresh wire instead of moving the existing one.
